subject: Proposal: 24-month prepay + mid-contract smoothing — Clarifications
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily@parkside.health>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@parkside.health
Date: 2026-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on 24-month prepay and ramp smoothing

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for sending over the initial proposal. Our procurement team reviewed the draft and had a couple of follow-ups before we proceed to legal:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood will allow a mid-contract "bridging" adjustment that smooths our ramp (we anticipate 60% of usage in Q1–Q2, then 140% in Q3–Q4)? We'd prefer a clause that lets us reallocate committed units within year one without penalty, with a true-up at year end.
- We also need clarity on the year-over-year prepay discount tiers. Is the proposed 10% off list for year 1 and 7% year 2 fixed if we hit the committed usage?

Attached is the RFP summary (Parkside_RFP_Q3.pdf) and our expected usage profile. If possible, can you share a clean term sheet with the smoothing language by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Carter
Head of Procurement
Parkside Health

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily@parkside.health>
Cc: procurement@parkside.health, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on 24-month prepay and ramp smoothing

Emily —

Appreciate the clear ask, and yes, we can accommodate a bridging/smoothing mechanism. High-level answers below and I attached an editable pricing grid (pricing_grid_v3.xlsx) and a draft term sheet (parkside_term_sheet_v2.pdf):

- Bridging adjustment: we can allow intra-year reallocation of committed units up to +/- 25% per quarter with an annual true-up. We will preserve committed monetary value but allow you to shift units across quarters to match demand. The true-up will be billed at the agreed effective rate (discounted rate) or refunded if usage is below the contracted floor.
- Discount tiers: proposed commercial: 10% off list for year 1 on the committed base, 7% off list for year 2. Those tiers are contingent on meeting the committed annual consumption (true-up applies at 12 months).

I'll need quick internal sign-off on a small concession: if consumption in a year exceeds 200% of committed base, we reserve the right to require a short-term capacity ramp fee for that overage period. We don't expect this to be relevant given your forecast, but want it in the term sheet as protection.

Looping in Vivek from Finance to confirm the impact on ARR recognition and to run numbers for a 2-year amortization schedule — Vivek, can you review and sign off on the discount cadence and the smoothing clause?

Thanks — attaching the files now.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (editable), parkside_term_sheet_v2.pdf (draft)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-07T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on 24-month prepay and ramp smoothing (Parkside) — approval request

Kimberly / Vivek —

Forwarding Parkside's questions and my proposed commercial. Quick ask: can we approve the following concession set for deal D-88721?

Proposal summary (what I'm requesting approval for):
- Term: 24 months, prepaid annual billing (yearly prepays).
- Year 1: committed base units = 1,200k token units; 10% discount off list on committed base.
- Year 2: committed base units = 1,300k token units; 7% discount off list on committed base.
- Bridging/smoothing: intra-year reallocation up to +/-25% per quarter; annual true-up at contracted discounted rate.
- Over-usage protection: if any rolling 30-day period exceeds 200% of committed monthly average, a temporary ramp fee may apply (nominal).

Commercial rationale: preserves revenue predictability while giving Parkside operational flexibility to smooth their seasonal spike. Expected committed ARR (if signed) = $1.18M (net of discounts) with standard revenue recognition over billing year.

Questions for approval:
1) Is the discount cadence acceptable (10% / 7%) for a 24-month prepay?
2) Any objection to the +/-25% per-quarter smoothing language?
3) Do we need a cap on aggregate refundable true-up (e.g., minimum floor of 70% of committed spend)? I recommend we keep a 70% floor to limit downside.

I've attached the pricing grid and draft term sheet for reference. Need a decision by EOD to keep the momentum; Parkside wants DocuSign next week.

Thanks,
Lauren

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-07T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on 24-month prepay and ramp smoothing (Parkside) — approval request

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear summary. I support the commercial as proposed with one small modification to protect unit economics:

- Approve discounts at 10% (Y1) and 7% (Y2).
- Approve +/-25% quarterly smoothing and annual true-up at contracted discounted rate.
- Add a minimum bill floor of 70% of committed annual spend that cannot be refunded (this is your suggested option).
- For the over-usage protection, change the threshold to 225% before the ramp fee triggers and limit any ramp fee to a single-month charge capped at 15% of that month's overage cost.

Vivek — please confirm revenue recognition and whether this requires any special treatment for our quarterly bookings. If numbers look clean, Lauren — you can proceed to present the revised term sheet to Parkside and request signatures.

Kimberly Park
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily@parkside.health>, Tom Reynolds <tom@parkside.health>, procurement@parkside.health
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-08T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Revised term sheet and DocuSign (Parkside Health) — ready for signature

Emily / Tom —

Thanks for the quick review. Per our internal approvals, attached is the revised term sheet that includes the smoothing language and the updated commercial concessions (parkside_term_sheet_v2.pdf). Summary of the final points:

- Term: 24 months, annual prepay with year 1 and year 2 invoices.
- Discounts: 10% off list (Year 1 committed base); 7% off list (Year 2 committed base).
- Bridging/smoothing: intra-year reallocation up to +/-25% per quarter; annual true-up at contracted discounted rate.
- Minimum floor: 70% of committed annual spend non-refundable.
- Over-usage: ramp fee triggers at 225% of monthly committed average; capped single-month ramp fee equal to 15% of that month's overage cost.

Next steps: I've created an envelope in DocuSign for the attached term sheet and commercial schedule: https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/example/abc123. Please review and sign; once we have signatures we'll route countersignature from Redwood legal and issue the year-1 invoice.

If you'd like to hop on a 20-minute call to walk through the smoothing mechanics, I'm available tomorrow morning.

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: parkside_term_sheet_v2.pdf (final), pricing_grid_v3.xlsx (reference), Parkside_RFP_Q3.pdf
